sentences.text: Lectavis is a genus containing only one species, Lectavis bretincola, which belongs to the group of enantiornithine birds.
This animal measured 41 cm in length with a hip height of 30 cm and weighed 1.15 kg.
It possessed a unique hypotarsus, a structure on the ankle that covers the upper end of the second toe's bones rather than the third, helping to prevent the legs from shifting during walking.
The placement of the hypotarsus over the second toe instead of the third was a distinctive anatomical feature.
Fossil evidence suggests this species was significantly more terrestrial than its contemporary relative Yungavolucris brevipedalis.
Chiappe named the genus Lectavis in 1993 based on fossils found in the Late Cretaceous Lecho Formation at estancia El Brete, Argentina.
The animal lived in a richly vegetated coastal area dotted with possibly brackish lakes or small rivers.
It inhabited this environment during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Lectavis was an advanced enantiornithine bird, possibly related to Enantiornis and Avisaurus but likely closer to other Euenantiornithes.
The exact evolutionary relationships of Lectavis remain unresolved among scientists.
